title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
abstract: arXiv:2611.25236v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Unplanned 30-day readmissions among patients with diabetes mellitus impose a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet most predictive models use only structured electronic health record (EHR) data and ignore free-text clinical notes, which often contain code-mixed Hindi-English (Hinglish) phrasing and negation that general-purpose language models parse unreliably. We propose a neurosymbolic multimodal framework evaluated on the public Diabetes 130-US Hospitals dataset (101,766 encounters; 71,518 patients) with a patient-level grouped 80/20 split. Three streams are fused: engineered structured features; 32 components of Bio_ClinicalBERT note embeddings obtained by truncated singular value decomposition; and symbolic entities extracted by an open-weight clinical language model within a three-stage hybrid retrieval-augmented generation pipeline (dense retrieval, sparse lexical retrieval, and cross-encoder re-ranking) with reflective ne

translated_title: 一种用于30天糖尿病再入院预测的神经符号多模态框架：整合结构化电子健康记录数据、密集临床嵌入与知识支撑的符号抽取
translated_abstract: 糖尿病患者的非计划性30天再入院会带来沉重的临床与经济负担，然而大多数预测模型仅使用结构化电子健康记录（EHR）数据，而忽略了自由文本临床笔记——这些笔记中常包含印地语-英语混杂（Hinglish）的表达以及否定结构，通用语言模型难以对其进行可靠解析。我们提出了一种神经符号多模态框架，并在公开的糖尿病130家美国医院数据集（101,766次就诊；71,518名患者）上进行了评估，采用患者级别的分组80/20划分。该框架融合了三种数据流：人工设计的结构化特征；通过截断奇异值分解获得的Bio_ClinicalBERT临床笔记嵌入的32个分量；以及由开放权重的临床语言模型在三阶段混合检索增强生成流水线（密集检索、稀疏词法检索与交叉编码器重排序）中抽取的符号实体，并带有反思性……（摘要至此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种神经符号多模态框架，将结构化EHR特征、Bio_ClinicalBERT临床笔记密集嵌入与基于三阶段混合检索增强生成流水线抽取的符号实体相融合，以更准确地预测糖尿病患者的非计划30天再入院风险。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a neurosymbolic multimodal framework that fuses structured EHR features, dense Bio_ClinicalBERT clinical note embeddings, and symbolic entities extracted through a three-stage hybrid retrieval-augmented generation pipeline to more accurately predict unplanned 30-day diabetic readmissions.
